Breaking: GTA 6 Metacritic User Scores Go Live, Resulting In Mass Review Bombing

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that after an incredibly long wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has dropped to massively positive reviews from critics, who have repeatedly described Rockstar's latest release as one of, if not the best games ever made.
  • Despite taking the industry by storm and boasting sales that broke a new record for the entertainment industry, GTA 6's review rating has just plummeted on Metacritic immediately after the site opened its user scores.
  • As noted by customers like CharlieIntel on X, while there are plenty of user reviews that note the flaws while celebrating its achievements, the User Review section for GTA 6 on Metacritic has been absolutely flooded with overwhelmingly negative reviews, many of which are from players who admit they "haven't even played the game" themselves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after an incredibly long wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has dropped to massively positive reviews from critics, who have repeatedly described Rockstar's latest release as one of, if not the best games ever made. While there was plenty of debate over whether the critic reviews and player responses would actually line up or not when it released, the public response has been almost equally impressive so far.

Despite taking the industry by storm and boasting sales that broke a new record for the entertainment industry, GTA 6's review rating has just plummeted on Metacritic immediately after the site opened its user scores.

As noted by customers like CharlieIntel on X, while there are plenty of user reviews that note the flaws while celebrating its achievements, the User Review section for GTA 6 on Metacritic has been absolutely flooded with overwhelmingly negative reviews, many of which are from players who admit they "haven't even played the game" themselves.

With GTA 6 presently sitting at a 5.1 user score at the time of writing, over half of the reviews uploaded for the game are negative, with countless politically charged reviews calling it "woke slop" and a "cuck simulator" over its relationship gameplay mechanics, or consumers straight-up keyboard-smashing negative reviews just so they can contribute to tearing down the game's score.

While it isn't exactly surprising that one of the most widely talked about games in history would wind up being the target of annoyed players or internet trolls wanting to join in on the fun, Take-Two had already expressed their concern about this exact situation happening years before GTA 6 released.

Even Nintendo's recently released Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake wasn't exempt from the same fate either, with Link's return being slammed by players in response to the game's popularity, rather than the actual quality of the remake.

Considering that there are some genuine complaints to be had surrounding GTA 6's console performance, control scheme, or returning franchise features that are currently absent in the newest release, it's hard to pinpoint what the actual score will end up being after the dust of its release settles.

If the critic scores and the Metacritic rating for Rockstar's previous games are anything to go by, however, Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely wind up with an incredibly high score regardless of the current review bomb storm, especially as the game gets even bigger with the eventual PC port and multiplayer release.

Nioh 3 is, unsurprisingly, the fastest-selling game in the series with over a million units sold

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit.
  • Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has revealed that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5.
  • Sources indicate that as a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has revealed that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

Sources indicate that as a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

Industry observers note that on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still demonstrates that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Sources indicate that nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since we're already sharing trailers from non-Geoff awards highlights, here's another: a first in-motion look at Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh, a 2D side-scroller and "lite-vania" that sees its shy witch-in-training making her first summonable friends. Then, borrowing their powers to bust out of a dark fantasy oubliette.

It looks like this'll be a mix of passively familiar-enhanced punching and more active, mayhaps traditionally Metroid-y power upgrades, Lola's ghastly pals looming over her tiny frame when called upon. It's all presented in a hand-drawn, lightly anime-ish style, complete with a story setup straight out of Saturday morning TV – Lola's only stuck in Skullcatraz because of a summoning-gone-wrong that occurred in pursuit of her school's unlikely Ofsted-compliant 'familiar contest'. I've attended school several times, and will attest that non-sporting contests, which students remain unaware of until seeing a poster for them, do not exist outside of childrens' television*.

This doesn't seem to be kid fodder, though. Lola's a bean but the familiars, and the prison's other denizens, are growling towers of jaws and decaying flesh. Developers Caracal Games are promising they'll star in a "heartfelt and emotionally resonant story about growth," to balance out the grimness, though I'm less clear on a following blurb point that declares it a "lite-vania," into which you'll "dive into exploration, trial-and-error and platforming, without feeling frustrated." While this might just be an attempt to assuage fears that this'll a Hollow Knight- or Nine Sols-style controller-thrower, I do wonder how one goes light on 'vania. Maybe some of the ability gates open if you just ask them nicely?

Industry observers note that that aside, I'm already quite charmed by Lola's Familiars, especially the designs of its bag-eyed wallflower of a heroine and her contrastingly hench minions. Release date is TBC, but the Steam page is up.

*Granted, no TV example was ever as egregiously misleading as Jack Black vehicle School of Rock, which convinced me - then a barely-pubescent aspiring bassist - that winning a local Battle of the Bands would pay out thousands in cash, as opposed to the drinks rounds and packs of guitar strings I'd end up competing for a few years later.

Breaking: The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an upgrade on what to expect in 2026

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to enhancement the community on what to expect in 2026.
  • The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to enhancement the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one patch on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s fresh blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

It has been revealed that the first stage of the newly introduced roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

Recent findings suggest that the infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo complications, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more concerns join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Recent findings suggest that until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more!

In a recent development, I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

In a recent development, conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past.".

Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Industry observers note that overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

  • Unlike, say, Postal II, there's no wackiness or crass humour here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there are plenty of controversial game franchises out there. But many are pretty lazy, and either intentionally racist, sexist or simply provocative. A truly controversial series is one that sets out to do something, and does so in an unapologetic and probably disturbing way. In unrelated news, Running With Scissors' Postal Classic & Uncut is out now on Google Play!

Unlike, say, Postal II, there's no wackiness or crass humour here. The story is simple: You are the Dude, and everybody else has to die. That means blasting your way through dozens of levels ranging from suburban neighbourhoods to downtown metropolises, with a variety of firearms and explosives, as you face down police officers, armed residents and plenty of unarmed civilians caught in the crossfire.

The Earth is Hungry Postal is a series that, while I won't necessarily defend, I think everyone will agree has an undercurrent of potential. The original Postal veers between exciting and chilling, as each level is interspersed with the paranoid ramblings of the Dude. And while the official story may be that you're defending yourself against crazed gunmen, all those people running for their lives may beg to differ.

In other words, you're stepping into the disturbed mind of a crazed gunman. Not hard to see why this was so controversial back in the day.

Recent findings suggest that it's a thoroughly dark, brooding and unnerving concept, and one that Running With Scissors are revisiting in the upcoming Flesh & Wire, a more horror-focused FPS set in the aftermath of the Dude's rampage. Of course, if you strip all that away, Postal remains a pretty solid isometric shooter and a real 90s snapshot.

If you've got a strong stomach for it, you can find Postal Classic & Uncut available on Android, with all 16 original levels and four from the Special Delivery expansion included.

In a recent development, postal Classic & Uncut is definitely not a cheery game for the weekend. So if you need something a little calmer and more laid-back, why not check out our latest list of the five latest mobile games to try this week?

Industry observers note that download now! Postal Classic & Uncut.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
  • Sources indicate that hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
  • Industry observers note that the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

Sources indicate that hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

Industry observers note that the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

In a recent development, aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most hotly anticipated games of all time, and few things can slow down its momentum, thanks to the sheer hype and quality on display. The quickest thing to put a damper on excitement, sadly, is bugs, hiccups that are both unintended and hard to fix in any quick manner.

In a recent development, the streets of Leonida have been plagued by a number of minor graphical and physics bugs that have led to laughs, but one repeat offender is causing challenges for PS5 players. Internally titled error code CE-108255-1, this bug causes a no-frills, hard crash back to the PlayStation home screen after a brief play window, causing players to lose progress and time as they’re forced to reset.

For a massive open-world story game like Grand Theft Auto 6, forced short playtimes can be a killer, and the constant crashes forced by error code CE-108255-1 are causing just that. Complaints across the internet say the error has no discernible cause, but it only appears on PlayStation 5 systems, leaving Xbox players in the clear.

A recent set of firmware updates could be causing the error afflicting PS5 players, but neither Sony nor Rockstar has released any statement on it. Hopefully, as more players stumble into it, a swift hotfix patches the issue before too many lose potentially hours of playtime to a simple bug. GTA6’s robust simulation elements would make the loss even harder, taking tons of hard work with it.

No usual methods seem to help; reinstalling the game, going offline, and keeping the system cool all seem to be fruitless. Without a proper fix, players are stuck just hoping it doesn’t happen to them, a frustrating possibility that could easily tarnish their experience playing such an anticipated release.

The quickest thing to put a damper on excitement, sadly, is bugs, hiccups that are both unintended and hard to fix in any quick manner.

In a recent development, across the board, Grand Theft Auto 6 seems very well optimized, despite being trapped at 30 FPS across all platforms. A frame unlock is likely to come with the PC version, either officially or thanks to mods once the title jumps ship from consoles. Until then, fans are forced to pray and keep playing, crossing their fingers that their hard-earned cash isn’t lost due to the whims of an error they can’t avoid.

Over the last decade or so, a number of massive AAA titles have been released frankly unfinished. With Cyberpunk 2077 as the biggest offender, players have gotten sick and tired of being forced to shuffle through mountains of bugs and errors in order to play the games they pay for.

That makes Grand Theft Auto 6’s error code CE-108255-1 all the more frustrating; with how well polished the vast majority of the experience is, a hiccup like this sticks out like a sore thumb. The fine folks at Rockstar have clearly spent over a decade of blood, sweat, and tears to make Grand Theft Auto 6 the powerhouse it is, and losing face because of a bug like this is just sad.

With no acknowledgement from the studio yet, fans are left to their own devices, and some have gotten more than a little spiteful.

Recent findings suggest that no physical copy, a $79.99 base price tag, and multiple on-disc locations barred behind a special edition give GTA6 an outer coat that has nothing to do with its criminal focus. It feels like the industry is yet again at a tipping point set by a major player, with the future in the hands of the rest of the AAA developers surrounding them.

It has been revealed that look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a upcoming Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month! This class is called the Sisters Novitiate, a group of wonderfully violent women with a penchant for crossbows, burning people alive and putting a stop to anyone that dares to oppose the God-Emperor. Neato!

Recent findings suggest that according to a blog post accompanying the reveal of the class, the Sisters Novitiate work a tad differently compared to other classes available in the game. "Unlike other classes, the Sisters Novitiate are able to choose from six divine and devastating Acts of Faith, as opposed to blitz and combat abilities," the post explains. "Their abilities draw upon reserves of Faith, allowing them to unleash brutal Neural Whip attacks to the inspiring Icon of Purity and protective prayers. Faith can take many forms for the Sisters Novitiate, each channeling the Emperor's divine will and bringing his wrath upon his enemies.".

You build up their Faith while fighting, in turn choosing from a selection of doctrines and pledges in their talent tree, "each shaping how Faith is both accumulated and put to use. Any two Acts of Faith can be equipped at a time, allowing players to choose how their Novitiate will unleash righteous fury on the battlefield." I mentioned crossbows, right? Well, I stand lore corrected, as what they technically have is the Condemnor Stakethrower, which "pins what remains of their enemies to the walls." They do also have access to a flamethrower, a big ole mace, your classic sword and shield, and whatever the hell a "Penitent Eviscerator.".

Sources indicate that this DLC class also comes the same day as a free upgrade, which will introduce the Metlagun, equipable by the Sisters Novitiate as well as the Veteran. Apparently there'll be more information on the free update soon. Oh, and the release date! It's December 7th, so a little under a month away. I'm sure you can (Dark)tide over the next few weeks by rewatching the gnarly reveal trailer.

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (360 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie?
  • The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history.
  • Sources indicate that beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with.

Industry observers note that is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's vital because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Sources indicate that beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history.".

Perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

How To Deposit Money In A Bank Account In GTA 6

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (413 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Living in Leonida isn't cheap, and being a wanted criminal doesn't mean you get to skip the boring financial stuff.
  • Sources indicate that getting your finances in order doesn't require a business degree or a meeting with your accountant.
  • Industry observers note that to get a bank account in GTA 6, you'll first need to progress through the main story until you get Lucia out of jail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Living in Leonida isn't cheap, and being a wanted criminal doesn't mean you get to skip the boring financial stuff. If you've been trying to treat yourself to some newly introduced clothes or other goodies in GTA 6, you might have run into a rather annoying little problem: some stores won't let you shop without a bank account. Rude!

Sources indicate that getting your finances in order doesn't require a business degree or a meeting with your accountant. You'll just need to get familiar with the game's banking system and figure out how to manage your cash. Here's everything you need to know to get your money situation sorted.

Industry observers note that to get a bank account in GTA 6, you'll first need to progress through the main story until you get Lucia out of jail. Shortly afterward (the day after the first night, in fact), she will call you, asking you to open a bank account.

Sources indicate that you'll then visit a bank and speak with the manager, who will explain that he can't open a traditional account for you. Instead, he'll direct you to the BuckMe application. During the cutscene, you'll automatically open the app and set up your account.

Once BuckMe is unlocked, you can deposit your cash at ATMs and use your bank balance to purchase items that require a bank account.

In a recent development, to find the nearest ATM, pull out your phone by pressing up on the D-pad and open the BuckMe application. Select the ATM Locations option (by scrolling down) using the D-pad, and the closest ATM will be marked on your map.

In a recent development, drive to the location and interact with the ATM to deposit the cash you're carrying into your BuckMe account. You can then use those funds to purchase items at stores that require a bank account.

It has been revealed that buckMe also gives you access to a Family Savings account, which you can transfer money into directly through the application. You'll need to deposit $5,000 into Family Savings to progress through a later quest, so make sure you set aside some money for it while keeping enough in your regular account for shopping.

Sources indicate that some items can still be purchased with physical cash, so you don't need to deposit everything you earn. However, getting BuckMe set up early will make shopping and managing your money much easier throughout GTA 6.

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another newly introduced entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

It has been revealed that that said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Sources indicate that speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

According to recent reports, the game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

Recent findings suggest that you can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite quickly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

For starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Recent findings suggest that different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create latest effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next major game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

Sources indicate that the Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two latest features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

Sources indicate that the Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

According to recent reports, created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

In a recent development, it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

According to recent reports, in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

According to recent reports, in the blog post announcing the newly introduced features, Maxis noted that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

Industry observers note that "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the manufacturer's future.

Recent findings suggest that the Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the manufacturer, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a upcoming game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Industry observers note that alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

In a recent development, "While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

Recent findings suggest that that certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent company Microsoft are still right now subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that whenever I mention that I write about mobile gaming, the inevitable first response from laymen and industry people alike is, 'Well, that's all just gacha, right?' And on the one hand, they're not necessarily right, but not wrong either. The random draw system is so pervasive that even many developers pit themselves against it, like with the upcoming Mixcity Swap.

Positioning itself as the anti-gacha, Mixcity Swap is an upcoming sports-themed card battler by Atypique Studio, releasing in 2027 for iOS and Android, that sees you taking on fast-paced, 10-minute matches. With only nine cards on the roster, the gameplay revolves around swapping in and out your athletes across different modes, doing so at the right interval as they activate their individual effects.

In that way, I think positing it as anti gacha is a bit of a misnomer. At its core, Mixcity Swap looks to be an exciting standalone card game, and one that doesn't really need to pit itself against such a widely reviled mechanic to be successful.

According to recent reports, but, I'll certainly be interested to see how Atypique intends to grow this game in future. We've got plenty of small-scale card battlers that avoid gacha, but a long-term live-service type release may be a very different beast to keep loyal to that ideal.

Still, if you find yourself wanting more card-battling action on mobile, then you're not without plenty of options to try. Just take a look at our list of the best card battlers on iOS, and you'll find some choice picks you can play right now!

#40521. What Is The Day/Night Cycle Length In GTA 6?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

What Is The Day/Night Cycle Length In GTA 6?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (418 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every day in Grand Theft Auto 6 is relatively long, but it's not as long as real life.
  • The same goes for days that are too long, though, since it wouldn't be realistic for it to take only an hour or so to drive all the way around the entire state.
  • Sources indicate that every minute in Grand Theft Auto 6 lasts for five real seconds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every day in Grand Theft Auto 6 is relatively long, but it's not as long as real life. A day has to be long enough to do some of the many things in the game, but it also has to reflect the size of the map. If you drove from one end of the map to the other, it wouldn't be realistic if it took you multiple days just to drive across the city.

The same goes for days that are too long, though, since it wouldn't be realistic for it to take only an hour or so to drive all the way around the entire state. Luckily, we did the math to determine just how long a day is in Leonida.

Sources indicate that every minute in Grand Theft Auto 6 lasts for five real seconds. That means every hour lasts 300 seconds, or five real-life minutes. With the same conversion for a 24-hour day, multiply that five minutes by 24, and you find that a full 24-hour cycle in the game lasts for two real-life hours.

According to recent reports, this is significantly longer than a day in Grand Theft Auto 5, which lasted 48 real-life minutes. The scaling makes sense, though, because the map size matches each day's length. If a day in GTA 5 lasted as long as it did in GTA 6, you could've crossed the map multiple times in a single cycle.

While you can't directly speed up the clocks, you can skip chunks of time if you don't want to be out at a certain time. If you go to bed, you can choose to sleep, and setting your alarm will determine what time of day it is when you get up.

Industry observers note that you can set the alarm for morning, noon, evening, or night. It doesn't matter what time you go to sleep; you can sleep until any time of day. If it's earlier than it currently is, it will move on to the next in-game day. That way, if you have tasks that depend on a certain time of day or require you to wait for the next day, you can skip the wait.

Luckily, there's plenty to do day or night in this game, and certain events only happen at certain times. It's good to know you can skip time if you need to, but there are lots of reasons to enjoy the day/night cycle to the fullest.

  • In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our fresh galactic overlords!".

But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

According to recent reports, offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Sources indicate that outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is presently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

It has been revealed that patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

Industry observers note that when you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the newly introduced Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies promptly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a latest activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

In a recent development, anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

In a recent development, there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a upcoming item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Sources indicate that even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the newly introduced season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the latest class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Industry observers note that season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

Industry observers note that the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

Recent findings suggest that that latest patch was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page right now indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of problems.

"We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the glitch," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.".

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there right now looks to have been no significant hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

It has been revealed that the debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

📅 06 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (422 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Patch, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.
  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.
  • Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Patch, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

In a recent development, the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

It has been revealed that the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside upcoming Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Recent findings suggest that lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the substantial day.

#40514. Industry News: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3428 w)
