Tech Report: I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
  • Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did.
  • Industry observers note that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that massive a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.

Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did. GTA 5 is an exotic and sun-kissed heist movie, a mould that GTA 6’s tale of gun-toting love in Vice City very much looks to follow. That leaves Sleeping Dogs protagonist Wei Shen standing next to Niko Bellic. One might be kicking faces in Hong Kong and the other might be getting into shootouts in New York, but both are fresh off the boat in places both familiar and alien. They find themselves caught between two lives.

Industry observers note that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop. For Niko, it’s a balancing act between trying to settle old scores and start a fresh life in post 9/11 America. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a pork bun to chow down on. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a hotdog to chow down on. Both of their games are beloved for delivering tales which get the player invested in Wei and Niko specifically, that excel in putting you into the emotional shoes of these two underworld operators whose worlds are tearing at them from multiple angles as they claw their way to the top of the food chain.

Industry observers note that despite my headline gag, they do this with a comparably minimal amount of in-depth life-simmy details, like those that’re baked into Red Dead Redemption 2 (and GTA 6, to a degree) as some of the main selling points. Wei can buy a pork bun, the vendor loudly informs him that by doing so he’s avoiding the possibility of never becoming a whole man, but there’s no ‘whole manliness’ meter which demands to be satiated with regular pork bun munching, lest Wei become a less than whole man. All it does is give him a temporary health regeneration boost, because as we all know, the first thing the doctors do if you’re admitted to hospital with grievous wounds after a fight is serve you a scrumptious meal that miraculously closes up your cuts in minutes.

Sleeping Dogs dedicates all of its life simming effort to making you feel the weight of Wei’s torment as he grapples with an unsustainable double life of sinning and saintly acts. Like GTA 4, it’s not got the time, tech, or budget to adorn itself with animations or systems that replicate every aspect of Wei’s day-to-day existence in excruciating detail. It’s simply assumed, rather than demonstrated, that some of the back alleys he wanders down to bust drug dealers probably smell a bit unpleasant. He doesn’t have over 60 species of bird to catalogue as he commutes from North Point to the businessman-infested Central district, then on to the houseboat-heavy Aberdeen and gated communities of Kennedy Town. Though, he does keep nicking jade statues, in order to persuade his kung fu instructor to teach him some fun fresh ways to knee baddies into submission.

He can sing his lungs out to nail I Fought the Law at one of Hong Kong’s few karaoke booths or lose all of his cash playing mahjong, but he doesn’t have an endless laundry list of optional hobbies long enough to suck players who aren’t even particularly trying to get distracted in for hundreds of hours.

Then again, if he wanders into his Central apartment, Wei can take a piss. In truth, I’d forgotten about this prior to my recent revisit, but it is a wonderfully simple feature that really emphasises how things’ve changed for games like these in the years since 2012. I press one button when the prompt pops up near the loo, and Wei unzips before dribbling a rather loud trickle into the bowl. Then, he’s done. I can get him to wash his hands if I wish, but no bladder meter has gone down and no dirtiness meter is being satiated by my scrubbing. If Wei doesn’t take regular whizzes, no NPCs comment that he’s looking a bit pained, and his walking animation doesn’t dynamically adjust to huddle his legs closer together.

You could ask what was even the point of animating Wei’s pissing if it’s a pointless and totally optional activity, outside of arguably doing a tiny bit of work in helping Shen be convincingly human (and it unquestionably being quite funny the first time you stumble across it). By looping what would once have been one-note button presses into systems that help them play a more active role in fleshing out the world and the routines of its inhabitants, uber-detailed games like GTA 6 - at their best - add an extra layer of definition to the tales and adventures they depict.

It has been revealed that they often feel like the sort of game Sleeping Dogs might’ve been if it’d had their tech and its budget was the GDP of real world Hong Kong. The question is, when limitations like that don’t apply to the degree they once did, where the line lies between extra layers which tangibly deepen the player’s experience and overindulgent bloat?

Sleeping Dogs, despite working in its own takes on elements of GTA, Saints Row, and I’d argue RGG Studio’s earlier Like A Dragon/Yakuza entries, is an unquestionably lean and focused game. Less isn’t necessarily more, especially if you were to ask slumbering canines-loving teenage me, who would’ve bitten your hand off for Hong Kong to boast even a third of the extra features and activities GTA 6 and Red Dead 2 pack into their life of crime sims.

Industry observers note that the latter two are games that wouldn’t have been possible to make, at least in a format the masses would be able to play, back in the era when Sleeping Dogs and GTA 4 represented what an open-world crime game typically looked like. They’ve eaten up what used to be the domain of arcade racers like Midnight Club and hunting sims to step closer to being something reminiscent of Better Than Life, the addictive VR everything game from the Red Dwarfverse, which takes over players’ lives by simulating a world where everything they want can play out in reality-mimicking detail.

They aim to be far, far more than what defined their predecessors, and to use that to appeal to an ever-expanding audience. What I’m intrigued to see, whenever I get my hands on Rockstar’s latest work, is whether those like me who come to it having recently played a game like Sleeping Dogs will find a game that feels like it’s being pulled in a million different directions, to the point that it loses something of what historically has been at the centre of its fundamental appeal.

Or, to put it another way: is there a point at which you’ve eaten so many pork buns in one sitting that you begin to stray away from the self-actualisation which steady consumption of them is known to facilitate?

Simply put, Xbox and Bethesda are teaming up with the developers behind games such as A Building Full of Cats to create a Wasteland-themed game where you'll seemingly have to locate cats throughout the Fallout universe.

In other words, this would appear to be a hidden object game.

We'll throw some footage of one of this developer's Xbox titles down below so you can get an idea of what to expect. Their games are also always very inexpensive, and they also have some fantastic reviews on the Xbox Store.

Sources indicate that there's obviously lots of other Fallout stuff in the works right now, including two remasters based on Fallout 3 and Fallout: Fresh Vegas, as well as the much-anticipated Fallout 5. This new "inspired" game clearly just serves as a bit of fun to plug the gap, and we reckon it might actually do very well when it debuts in the future.

It's cool to see Xbox partnering on lighthearted ideas like this! Long may it continue - do it with Halo and Gears next?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyberagent - the parent company of Umamusume: Pretty Derby developer Cygames - has boasted its recent successes in the mobile gaming sphere in a recent quarterly earnings presentation.

As part of this presentation (covered by Automaton), the organization has established plans to launch seven "major releases" to the mobile platform by 2030. There is no word on what these games will be, but one will be released in 2027, while another two will come in 2028.

Industry observers note that cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. Those games include Umamusume: Pretty Derby, Final Fantasy Ever Crisis, Hololive Dreams, and Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade.

In a recent development, cyberAgent CEO Takahiro Yamauchi - speaking during the presentation - noted that it was still difficult to predict the success of a mobile game ahead of its release. However, he also claims that the experience Cyberagent has gained with its big releases to date have allowed the tech giant to gain a clearer perspective on profitability and sustainability.

In a recent development, this presentation comes after a notable month for Cygmes and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The developer issued refunds for hotels and flights following the sudden cancellation of an LA live show for the game last month, then shortly after became a major sponsor of the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix. The game was also temporarily taken offline due to the major PHP vulnerability exposed last month, an outage that was thankfully short-lived.

Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest update post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

Industry observers note that in addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by Fresh Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

Other than these new hires, the update is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

According to recent reports, the update is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but Upcoming Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hoYoverse just wrapped up a newly introduced Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major upgrade. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

It has been revealed that if you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this revision. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter rapidly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”.

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Recent findings suggest that her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

According to recent reports, lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second newly introduced character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Sources indicate that through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Recent findings suggest that nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a upcoming limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

It has been revealed that one newly introduced gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

Corsair Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo review

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2188 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the aim-assisting PureVector technology in this mouse promises a lot, but in my case it fails to deliver, as my aim doesn't improve from turning it on.
  • Sources indicate that PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you.
  • In a recent development, corsair is continuing the 2026 trend of brands pushing out new and innovative mouse technologies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the aim-assisting PureVector technology in this mouse promises a lot, but in my case it fails to deliver, as my aim doesn't improve from turning it on. It's a solid, lightweight, competitive mouse regardless, but it's too expensive for what it is without delivering the PureVector promise.

Sources indicate that PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

In a recent development, corsair is continuing the 2026 trend of brands pushing out new and innovative mouse technologies. In this case, it's all in the 'PureVector' part of the name. In partnership with AimLabs, Corsair has made a mouse that can adjust sensitivity in different directions to tailor it to your movements and help you aim better.

According to recent reports, that's the claim, anyway. In practice, I've found that PureVector hasn't improved my aim, both subjectively while gaming and objectively based on multiple AimLabs tests. Some pro players that Corsair highlights claim it's helped them, so your mileage may vary.

In a recent development, apart from PureVector, though, the mouse itself deserves some attention, as it's still a very performant, lightweight mouse for competitive gaming. It has some upgrades compared to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro, too.

Industry observers note that ✅ You want to try the latest tech: You might get better results than I did with PureVector. It tailors sensor sensitivity in different directions based on how you aim.

❌ You want good value for the basics: If you just want a comfy mouse with solid build quality that performs well, you can find something of better value elsewhere.

Industry observers note that the aim-assisting PureVector technology in this mouse promises a lot, but in my case it fails to deliver, as my aim doesn't improve from turning it on. It's a solid, lightweight, competitive mouse regardless, but it's too expensive for what it is without delivering on the PureVector promise.

Replacement skates, USB-A to USB-C cable, wireless dongle, AimLabs PureVector software integration.

In most ways, the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is your standard competitive gaming mouse: lightweight, few frills, simple design, good sensor. It is lighter than most competitive mice with a solid shell, though a little heavier than its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro.

Setting aside the PureVector aiming shenanigans for a moment, probably the biggest improvement compared to the Sabre V2 Pro is its battery life, which has been doubled. Apart from that, you're getting a 42,000 DPI sensor, optical clicks, and some bigger replacement skates included in the box.

Now we come to the main attraction: PureVector. Corsair has designed the mouse's internals and firmware to permit different sensitivities in different directions. So, for instance, it can move slightly slower horizontally than vertically.

Corsair has worked with AimLabs to let you test your aiming in the latter software and then have the mouse adjust your directional sensitivity for you. The PureVector software within AimLabs has been made with the help of a bunch of aiming data (over 4 billion data points, apparently) and machine learning. The end result is, in theory, a mouse that can tailor its sensitivity in different directions to stop you over-shooting or under-shooting your target.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

Again, in theory, this should also save you time when you aim, and Corsair claims it can save more time than reducing the latency of clicks—the latter is, for example, what we see the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike and X3 Superstrike focusing on.

In a recent development, it's worth noting that Corsair highlights a number of pro players who say they've benefitted from this new tech. However, for my part, I haven't noticed a difference.

For reference, I play Counter-Strike 2 at about FaceIt Level 7 or Premier 18–20,000 rating (approx. top 15%). I'm far from a pro, but I'm far from the worst. In-game, I didn't notice any difference between my aim with PureVector set up and with it disabled.

I also repeatedly tested my aim in the AimLabs SpiderShot Precision test, and I actually had slightly better results using another mouse without PureVector (the SteelSeries Sensei Pro), and the latter mouse my hand was less familiar with.

According to recent reports, more than this, though, I can't help but feel that it's a bit of a band-aid solution to poor aim. If you're overshooting your shots when you aim left, for instance, you could get PureVector to lower your sensitivity in that direction. But why not instead work on training your hand not to overshoot? That way, having good aim won't be dependent on using this one mouse, and you can get used to aiming consistently in different directions.

It has been revealed that pureVector aside, the Sabre V3 Pro performs well. The sensor is great and feels very responsive. Ditto the fresh optical mouse clicks. I have no complaints about its performance as a general mouse, I just don't see the use in PureVector myself. Of course, your mileage may vary, as it seems to have for some pro players.

One area where the Sabre V3 Pro does particularly shine, just like the Sabre V2 Pro, is in its light weight. This latest iteration feels even sturdier than the previous one and still manages to be lighter than most competitive gaming mice.

It has been revealed that battery life is a definite selling point of the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector. It's a lot better than I was expecting. The Sabre V2 Pro can only manage about 70 hours at 1 kHz, and this latest one doubles that to 140 hours.

Industry observers note that I think Corsair has struck a great balance here, because it's not as light as the V2—which was 36 g—but 41 g is still incredibly light, and I'd much rather have the bigger battery than shave off those few extra grams. You're not getting any fancy wireless charging or hot-swappable batteries here, but 140 hours of battery life is great.

According to recent reports, the Corsair Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is, as its excruciatingly long name suggests, pretty ergonomic. It's not the biggest ergo mouse I've used—the Zowie EC2-DW and SteelSeries Rival Pro both feel a bit bigger in-hand—but it still feels comfy under my medium-sized palm.

There's also a non-ergo, symmetrical version for the same price, and you can get carbon fiber or magnesium versions for each, if you're willing to spend even more ($200 and $230, respectively).

I like the lightweight ergonomic version, though. Its slightly smaller size, combined with its light weight, also means holding it in a fingertip or claw grip doesn't feel too bad, which isn't something you can say about many ergonomic mice. Palm grip is still the main intention here, though. Playing Counter-Strike on low sensitivity feels great.

Build quality is decent, too, which is a bit of a relief because the previous version, the Sabre V2 Pro, sacrificed some on this front to achieve its 'ultralight' status. There's no creak or flex along the sides, and only a slight bit of flex on the underside. The side buttons feel great, with no pre-travel, and the scroll wheel has well-defined steps.

In a recent development, there is some pre-travel to the left- and right-mouse buttons, however, and they don't feel as satisfying to press as some other mice like the Razer Viper V4 Pro or SteelSeries Rival Pro. They're far from bad, just not quite up to the standard of some other expensive gaming mice I've tried.

In a recent development, the version I've got here, the 'Ergo' one, is pretty plain and looks quite similar to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro. It's plain white, with only some very subtle grey accents. I'm fine with that, as the focus is on performance and comfort.

Industry observers note that any extra aesthetic fancies are likely to add to the weight, which isn't worth the sacrifice for this kind of mouse. As with most ultralight mice, you know what you're getting aesthetically, and it's minimal.

This mouse uses the same software as the previous V2 Pro. What's noteworthy is the software is browser-based—there's no locally-installable app to use. That's mainly because you're expected to just set it and go, without returning to adjust things.

Industry observers note that you can set up profiles to toggle between DPI using a mouse button combination, however. And the web software can be used offline if you install it as an app in your browser, so internet outages shouldn't cause any problems.

Recent findings suggest that the web hub is basic but gets the job done. The battery indicator isn't very precise, only showing a tiny icon and no percentage numbers, but that's my only complaint.

It has been revealed that the AimLabs integration is perfectly fine, too. Assuming you've got it installed on Steam, you can allow the web hub to boot it up for you from there, or boot it up yourself. Once in, you can navigate to PureVector and let it run you through the aim training to adjust your sensitivity in different sweep directions. It's intuitive, and the directional charts it shows are clear enough.

At $180/£160, the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is an expensive mouse. It joins the likes of the G Pro X2/X3 Superstrike, Viper V4 Pro, DeathAdder V4 Pro, SteelSeries Rival Pro, and other high-end, competitive gaming mice.

Can it compete with these? In my opinion, not quite. These other gaming mice each have extra features and new technologies that go some way towards justifying the very high price tags. The Superstrikes have analogue clicks, the Viper V4 Pro has FrameSync, the Rival Pro has hot-swappable batteries and UWB connectivity.

Sources indicate that the DeathAdder V4 Pro doesn't have anything too fancy like that, but is a very solid gaming mouse. I'd class the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector in this category, alongside the DeathAdder. That's because while the PureVector technology is indeed very upcoming, I haven't found it to have much of an impact, and so I'm left considering its merits as a general competitive gaming mouse, setting aside this new aim assist tech.

There are merits to it that justify a price tag above $100: light weight, comfy ergonomic shape, optical clicks, responsive scroll wheel, great battery life. But not enough to justify $180—not without something extra, which PureVector promises but, in my case, fails to deliver. Unless, that is, you're set on getting a mouse as light as this one is that still has a sturdy shell.

In a recent development, you could instead, for instance, go for something like the Mchose K7 V2 Ultra+ for about $90. Or a Pulsar mouse like the Pulsar X2 CrazyLight for $130, which sometimes drops to about $100 on sale.

If you fancy spending the extra to try it out for yourself and see if you can get the kinds of benefits the pros that Corsair highlights espouse, go for it. But for my money, I'd be opting for a cheaper lightweight mouse, or one with better build quality like the Viper V4 Pro.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we've been keeping an eye out for news of Nintendo's playable and electric ocarinas going on sale in Europe for a good while now. It looks like sales are just around the corner, but you're going to need to jump through some hoops if you want to get your hands on one.

Both the Nintendo playable model and HORI electric version will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. You can register your interest in getting either model now on the Nintendo website, but there are some criteria that you'll have to pass first.

Recent findings suggest that firstly, you'll need to have a Nintendo account registered in Europe (excluding Norway, Russia and South Africa), have allowed Nintendo to process your usage information to customise services, offers and recommendations in your Nintendo Account settings, and have allowed Nintendo to send email recommendations about games, events, special offers and more. You'll need to have done all of that by 22nd November.

You can only register your interest if you have "reached at least 10 hours of play time in the Nintendo Switch 2 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by 18/11/2026" using the same Nintendo account you use to register.

It has been revealed that and that's just to get an invite. On the day that the products become available, those who are invited will receive an email with a link to purchase either ocarina (limited to one each per customer).

The playable ocarina will set you back £29.99, bundling the instrument with a wrist strap and sheet music for all of the in-game songs. HORI's electric option is a little more expensive at £41.99, but also comes with a dedicated stand.

The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" states Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC".
  • The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald.
  • "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald noted, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.".

It has been revealed that notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

"It's about deeper immersion," Ronald noted. "It is about leveraging newly introduced technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering.".

According to recent reports, while referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a significant reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years.".

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

It has been revealed that another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix blueprint, and something we've seen the manufacturer dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald stated. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players.".

Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely upcoming technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mainstay of the GTA series has been the presence of sex workers, but Rockstar Games has dropped this aspect for the newly released GTA 6.

As reported by Shack News, unlike most other games in the long-running franchise, you cannot hire a sex worker in GTA 6.

The outlet asked Rockstar about this decision, and received the following response:.

It has been revealed that "GTAVI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon - things like wanted system, the radio, robberies and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTAVI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story.".

So, in other words, sex workers aren't included this time around because it wouldn't make sense for Jason or Lucia to pursue that, as they're already in a relationship — and that's a big part of the story.

As mentioned, they have been present in the series since 2001's GTA 3, and this will be the first 3D game to exclude them.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is also the first game that centres on a couple, however, with the relationship between Jason and Lucia interwoven in the gameplay as well as being a key tenet of the narrative. It seems Rockstar didn't think sex workers would be conducive to this goal.

What are your thoughts on this? Tell us in the comments section below.

[source shacknews.com, via kotaku.com].

In a recent development, as initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

It has been revealed that this now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

It has been revealed that according to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find newly introduced work soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years.
  • The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts.
  • The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving upcoming content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

Sources indicate that the message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

It has been revealed that the running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

Sources indicate that the timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large patch for Mystic Messenger, which may include fresh content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very swiftly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without upcoming content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

Sources indicate that to find out how this dating system works, here’s a Mystic Messenger primer that explains it all. Once you’ve wrapped your head around it, you’ll no doubt want to pick the correct answers for every guest, and this guide will help you nail every one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good (and hilarious) folks over at HDTVTest have been looking at the HDR Calibration settings for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and they've discovered that the tool is actually slightly broken as things stand.

Some of the specifics go over my head a little bit to be honest, but in a nutshell, the figures that are displayed on the calibration tool don't fully translate into the game itself, leading to a potentially inoptimal picture.

As a result, they've published a newly introduced nine-minute video (which you can see up above) to explain the issues.

"The HDR calibration screen in GTA 6 can be misleading, because Rockstar's Max Brightness, Paper White and Black Levels settings interact in unexpected ways. To be clear, GTA VI's HDR rendering isn't broken… it's the calibration procedure that can give misleading results.".

The video goes step-by-step on how they analysed the issues and tried to figure out the best possible HDR settings for GTA 6, and while their tests aren't fully concluded yet (there's another video to come in the future where they try multiple consumer displays), they've shared their initial best settings for displays capable of 1,000 nits or brighter.

Here are those three settings, but again, keep in mind that your TV must be capable of 1,000 nits of brightness or more, and that certain smart TV features or special HDR settings on your TV itself may interfere with the results.

According to recent reports, if your display isn't capable of 1,000 nits, do a bit of Googling to try and find out the specifics for your TV/monitor, and then times that figure by two in-game. So, if you're working with a maximum of 600 nits, set the figure as 1,200.

Recent findings suggest that I have to be honest and say I'm not seeing a lot of difference here, but I've also got an old TV with a max brightness of just over 600 nits, not to mention I'm using a few image-altering features that may be playing havoc with the settings. It's also noted in the video that this is generally based on playing in the dark, rather than in a brightly-lit room.

According to recent reports, have a play for yourself and see what you think - there's clearly a lot of people who are very thankful for these settings on YouTube and beyond, so we wanted to at least make you aware of them. The reality is that you may need to still do a bit of tweaking to find the perfect sweet spot for your setup though.

120 hours in GTA 6: What's it really like to review the biggest entertainment event of the decade?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Except for a lucky few, the wait actually ended several weeks ago.
  • Industry observers note that josh's credentials are in little doubt.
  • When you're reviewing any video game, time is the biggest enemy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The wait for GTA 6 is finally over. Except for a lucky few, the wait actually ended several weeks ago. Early access for the purpose of reviewing GTA 6 kicked off in plenty of time to allow select press and creators to experience the game in full ahead of launch. One such early adopter was GamesRadar+'s Editor-in-Chief, Josh West, the writer responsible for our five-star GTA 6 review. For this member-exclusive article, I asked him to offer a peek behind the curtain about what it was like to cast a verdict on the biggest entertainment event of the decade.

Industry observers note that josh's credentials are in little doubt. He notes he's played every single GTA game - "yes, even the ones on PS1" - and that he attended the midnight launch of GTA 4. He also reviewed GTA 5 back in 2013, but says that was a uniquely stressful experience. While it was relatively easy to keep GTA 6 under wraps, during his venture to Los Santos, he says "I lived in a small shared house with five other people. Keeping the fact that I had a copy of the game weeks in advance a secret, in an environment where nobody knocked before entering a room, still stresses me out thinking about it today.".

When you're reviewing any video game, time is the biggest enemy.

Industry observers note that "Around 120 hours" of playtime was logged by GTA 6's in-game counter when Josh sat down to write his review, though he notes the PS5's internal clock had recorded "far longer" than that. A few-weeks-long runway might seem like plenty of time to check out even a game of that significant size, but once you've factored in the need to sleep, eat, and fulfil other "demands of life," Josh says finishing the review ahead of deadline remained "a bit of a highwire act.".

"Time is the biggest enemy," he says. The deadline around a big review is pretty firm, dictated by an embargo that no-one can publish ahead of, but which no-one wants to be stuck behind. That "does sometimes mean you aren't able to engage with a world in the way you would if you were playing in an everyday environment." With the clock ticking in real life, whiling away the hours just hanging out with Jason and Lucia is something you might not want to commit too much time to.

Recent findings suggest that that's particularly ironic in a game like this, where a non-trivial slice of gameplay does revolve around "sitting there with Lucia on the couch, watching TV indicates and playing in-universe video games." And as a double-whammy, investing in your downtime is a genuinely useful activity: Focus, Josh indicates, is the game's most useful skill, but it's also the hardest to upgrade, and doing so usually requires completing tasks that require some mental effort - playing minigolf, hitting the shooting range, meditating, fishing. These all take up valuable review time, but they're also a pivotal part of the game experience that can't be skipped over if you want a full impression.

Despite being pushed towards the end by the hands of Father Time, Josh notes there's plenty left to see: "Even with the story complete and 80% overall game completion, there's still so much of GTA 6 that I'm yet to see, discover, and master." Even once the review was filed and the game was out, he was "exploring some corner of the map that you'd honestly have no reason to go anywhere near," where "I got dragged into a weird and utterly wild scripted encounter that is among my favourites in GTA 6.".

As much as there's still stuff to discover in the wilds of Leonida after more than 120 hours, Josh claims he knew he was in for something special "just a few hours in." When I asked what the first sign that GTA 6 truly had 'the sauce' was, he pointed to an innocuous encounter in the Keys: "I spent what little cash I had to make modifications to JAson's old Vapid '70 Ganado - new paint, new engine, the works. Within minutes of pulling out of the mod shop some random driver made an illegal turn and hit me. I pulled the car over to the side of the road, got out and started checking for damage, and got annoyed that the money was for nothing. It was at that point I realised I had been fully captured by this virtual reality, and that feeling never really went away.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

In a recent development, I'm GamesRadar's Managing Editor for news, shaping the news strategy across the team. I started my journalistic career while getting my degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick, where I also worked as Games Editor on the student newspaper, The Boar. Since then, I've run the news sections at PCGamesN and Kotaku UK, and also regularly contributed to PC Gamer. Can GTA 6 make $2 billion in its opening weekend? One industry analyst has run the numbers, and seems to think so

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right?
  • At least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter.
  • Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the manufacturer's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

At least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two announces opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the manufacturer's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

It has been revealed that we also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

"That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen stated, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow.".

But it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play.".

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

It's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

According to recent reports, steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated releases, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

It has been revealed that that version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

According to recent reports, all of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

In a recent development, steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Recent findings suggest that forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a newly introduced chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

It has been revealed that mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

Sources indicate that the Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

Industry observers note that the benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Recent findings suggest that version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a newly introduced Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can strategy where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

Sources indicate that there’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

Industry observers note that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers.".

Sources indicate that alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

So, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any concerns, over at its dedicated website.

According to recent reports, if you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, looks changed, and CD Projekt Red later revealed that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

It has been revealed that this isn't the first substantial bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a latest mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I just found a curious artifact of the Old West in GTA 6, and the best part is I stumbled across it completely by accident.

That's right, partner: Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and you won't find it in some trendy Western fashion shop or in a McMansion as part of a wealthy crypto bro's collection.

If you want to wear it yourself, I'll tell you below where you can find it.

I was out in Port Gellhorn looking for a particular kind of car for reasons completely unrelated to clothing accessories. While I was driving, I spotted a sign on the side of the road with a balloon tied to it, reading "Yard Sale" with an arrow pointing down the road.

Sources indicate that I followed the sign which led to more yard sale signs and, yup, sure enough, the signs pointed me to an actual yard sale. And among the items for sale was a very familiar-looking hat.

In a recent development, it's called a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" and, this being a yard sale, it only cost $5. But I knew the second I saw it that this was no ordinary cowboy hat. Here, have a look at it from the back.

In a recent development, yep. No mistaking that. I even got a little pang of sadness thinking about good ol' Arthur Morgan. I miss him. Maybe when I'm done with GTA 6, I'll strap on my spurs and take another ride through Red Dead Redemption 2.

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Recent findings suggest that directions: Head to Port Gellhorn. It's in Kelly County on the western side of the state along the coast. In the southern tip of Port Gellhorn, there's a small neighborhood of about five houses just northwest of the Dirt Merchants mod shop.

Look for the driveway filled with yard sale clutter: furniture and electronics and such. There's a bunch of balloons, a cut-out of a nearly naked cowboy, and a big American flag flying. You'll find the hat toward the back sitting on top of a guitar case on a couch. There's also a shirt, a cap, and some shoes for sale that definitely didn't belong to Arthur.

Sources indicate that the world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

In a recent development, available June 3 through July 29, the latest event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

Sources indicate that the developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:.

According to recent reports, episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Industry observers note that sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the latest content.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that with the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole fresh world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect.
  • Recent findings suggest that that add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game.
  • On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that with the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole fresh world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

Recent findings suggest that that add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

It's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

This is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators said in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it.".

According to recent reports, they aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

"Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month.".

Industry observers note that the battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both key to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later revision for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

WoW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of upcoming quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been a lot of talk around how long GTA fans have been waiting for the latest entry to launch, but Persona isn't actually that far behind. Persona 5 – in its original state – released over a decade ago on 15th September 2016, and although Persona 6 has now been officially unveiled, we're none the wiser as to when it will actually come out.

It's likely to finally land at some point in 2027 after the dust has settled from Persona 4 Revival, but according to a recent interview with general producer Kazuhisa Wada (thanks, Nintendo Everything), fans won't have to wait quite so long for the inevitable Persona 7.

Sources indicate that "We will continue to cherish what makes Persona unique, while also embracing changes in the times and needs, and taking on upcoming challenges. We aim to be a brand that can grow for 5, 10 years, and beyond.

"Among those projects, the one we’re currently working on is Persona 6. While there’s still limited information I can share, we want to prove the results of all the challenges we’ve faced so far through the game itself. With that in mind, we’re creating something even better than before, and we’re feeling a real sense of accomplishment as we work on it.

Sources indicate that "And Persona 6 is not the end. We are working on various things to ensure that you don’t have to wait as long for the next installment as we have in the past. And in order to make Persona an even bigger IP, we are constantly thinking about creative ideas and developments that will not disappoint your expectations. Please look forward to what’s to come from Persona.”.

Industry observers note that we will look forward to it, Wada-san, thank you sir. Let's keep the focus on Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 for now though, hm?

In a recent development, it's not a surprising statement, mind you. Game development is taking longer than ever these days, which also makes it more expensive than ever. So a lot of publishers are looking into potential solutions to cut down on dev time and increase the cadence of releases. As long as it doesn't involve handing everything off to AI, we're fine with that.

It has been revealed that persona 4 Revival is right now scheduled to launch on Switch 2 on 20th May 2027, a few months after other platforms. As for Persona 6, an imminent reveal has been rumoured recently thanks to a backend upgrade on the official website. Hardly concrete, but it's a start.

Industry observers note that what are your thoughts on Wada-san's comments here? Are you keen for the wait between mainline entries to be slightly shorter in the future? Let us know with a comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after years of dominating Netflix's top 10 list, Squid Game finally came to an end last year with its third and final season. But the story may not be over after all, as series creator Hwang Dong-hyuk indicates he might one day return to the franchise.

Industry observers note that "As far as I’m concerned, someday I’ll get back to Squid Game," remarked Hwang at the Doha Film Festival (Variety). "When I have a great idea, I’ll make another one." However, Hwang pointed out that he doesn't actually own Squid Game. "Unfortunately, it’s not mine… Netflix owns the IP, so it’s not my decision how to expand.".

Following a desperate man named Seong Gi-hun, who, alongside 455 other players strapped for cash, enters a deadly game to win a hefty prize, the dystopian series rapidly became a hit over at Netflix. The first season debuted to a near-perfect Rotten Tomatoes score, and the show is still Netflix's most-watched series ever, per Tudum.

Industry observers note that the idea for the series came to Hwang when he faced financial troubles of his own. "When I first wrote the script, the beginning point of my creative process was when I was poor," he said. "I didn’t have much money and imagined: What if it was me? Would I enter this kind of competition and try to win the prize? I was so broke in 2009. I was so broke. I only had like $5 in my account.".

According to recent reports, however, after the huge success of the first season, Hwang said he felt the pressure to make a second and third season just as good. "There was pressure from Netflix," added Hwang, "We were always getting questions: 'Where is Season 2? Season 3?' It was a nightmare.” However, Hwang said he never tries to "make something that people like," adding, "I always try to make what I like to make while at the same time hoping and praying people like what I like to make. If I lose that mindset, I’ll go crazy.".

According to recent reports, netflix already released the American reality show Squid Game: The Challenge based on the series. Soon after Squid Game season 3, the streamer also announced a US remake from Gone Girl director David Fincher, which was hinted at in the Squid Game season 3 ending featuring Cate Blanchett as the new recruiter. However, reports suggest that the show may now be dead.

You can stream Squid Game in full on Netflix now. For more, see where it places on our list of the best Netflix shows, and keep up with new TV shows on the way.
